git add -A && git commit -m "feat(runway-ops): wire validators + AuditSource union + auditObserver + extract fuzzy-match

Slack Modal Phase 0 / Builder 0b — operations-layer hardening per
pre-plan v7 §A1-§A4 + §Wave 0b.

What's new
- Wave 0b validators wired INSIDE every write helper (addProject,
  createWeekItem, createTeamMember, updateProjectField,
  updateWeekItemField). Modal, MCP, CLI, migration, and bot-direct
  paths all hit the same gate. Soundly's NaN/NaN render on 2026-04-29
  was the proximate cause — bad dates / bare resources / mismatched
  status+category were slipping through.
- New shared validators in operations-utils.ts:
  normalizeEmptyToNull, validateStatusCategoryCompatibility (L1 7-rule
  matrix), validateRoleTagOnResources, validateStartEndDateOrder,
  validatePastDateNonTerminal (soft-warn only), validateNotesMaxLength
  (L1=500 / L2=280).
- AuditSource TS union (slack-modal-bot | slack-modal-slash | mcp |
  bot-direct | migration | cli | null) + AuditEvent shape +
  formatModalUpdatedBy('slack:UID:modal[-edit]').
- auditObserver?: (event: AuditEvent) => void hook on every write
  helper. Wave 14 intercept-miss alert subscribes here without inline
  grep. Pre-modal-era callers omit it; observer is purely additive.
- src/lib/feature-flags.ts: isModalInterceptEnabled() reads
  process.env.MODAL_INTERCEPT_ENABLED === 'true'.
- src/lib/runway/fuzzy-match.ts: Sørensen-Dice extracted as a shared
  module. Builders 3, 8, 9, 11 import this for caller-side fuzzy match
  in route handlers without pulling the validator chain.
- INTERCEPT_ALLOWLIST + INTERCEPT_EXCLUDED constants + lint-guard test
  iterating bot-tools.ts source for /^create_/ tools.

Tests
- +93 net new tests; all 2245 pass; lint zero errors.
- operations-utils.test.ts: full validator coverage + matrix rules +
  formatModalUpdatedBy + intercept allowlist constants.
- operations-add / operations-writes-week / operations-writes-project /
  operations-writes-team .test.ts: validator rejection paths +
  auditObserver firing + source propagation.
- feature-flags.test.ts and fuzzy-match.test.ts cover all new modules.
- intercept-allowlist.test.ts is the lint guard.

Compat fixes (small)
- bot-hardening.test.ts F1: notes max test split into 'within cap'
  (500) and 'exceeds cap' (501). A5/B1 use role-tagged resources.
- 001-april-14-updates.ts archived migration: per-column replacement
  strings (owner stays bare; resources gets role prefix) so the now-
  wired role-tag validator accepts the historical migration's writes.

Out-of-scope follow-ups
- updateProjectField does not own status writes (separate
  updateProjectStatus path); category-field updates re-run the matrix
  vs current project.status. status writes through updateProjectStatus
  do not yet revalidate matrix — flag for Builder 0d sweep.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>"

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(inngest): proposal-expiry sweeper cron (every 15 min)

Adds `sweepExpiredProposals` Inngest function that runs every 15 minutes
against the Runway DB to enforce TTL on Slack modal proposals (per
slack-modal pre-plan v7 §"Wave 12").

Two named step.run blocks for durable retries:
- mark-expired: pending rows past expires_at -> status='expired',
  status_reason='TTL elapsed'.
- delete-stale-terminal: rows in any terminal status (submitted |
  cancelled | expired | failed) older than 24h are reaped to keep the
  proposals table small.

Idempotent — WHERE clauses are self-limiting, so re-runs against an
already-converged DB return zero counts. retries: 1, since the next
cron tick (<=15 min) will reconverge on transient failure.

Tests: 8 unit tests covering schedule registration, state transitions,
24h delete-cutoff window, idempotency, and step.run naming. Mocks the
runway db client + drizzle-orm helpers + the Inngest client (mirrors
runway-slack-message.test.ts pattern).

Note: `serve({ functions: [...] })` registration in
src/app/api/inngest/route.ts is intentionally NOT modified here per the
Builder 12 strict-scope mandate — the orchestrator or a follow-up
builder owns that wiring.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
